article.Citation/Title: Sessa, B., Higbed, L., O'Brien, S., Durant, C., Sakal, C., Titheradge, D., Williams, T. M., Rose-Morris, A., Brew-Girard, E., Burrows, S., Wiseman, C., Wilson, S., Rickard, J., & Nutt, D. J. (2021). First study of safety and tolerability of 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine-assisted psychotherapy in patients with alcohol use disorder. Journal of Psychopharmacology, 35(4), 375-383.
article.Outcome: 12/14 (85.7%) completed both MDMA sessions; 0 unexpected AEs
article.InterventionDescription: MDMA-assisted psychotherapy: 2 sessions (125mg oral + 62.5mg booster at 2hr; 187.5mg total each), within an 8-week, 10-session outpatient course post-detox.

ae_events.Description: Mild, transient rise in blood pressure, heart rate and temperature during MDMA dosing sessions; stayed within normal limits for all but one participant.
One participant's blood pressure rose to 183/118 two hours after initial MDMA dose, attributed to missed antihypertensive medication; asymptomatic, resolved spontaneously, booster dose withheld.
Mildly elevated Subjective Units of Distress (anticipatory anxiety) reported by most participants at session onset, reducing as MDMA's positive effects emerged.

article.Outcome: The article's stated main/primary outcome measures are safety and tolerability endpoints (Methods: 'number of patients completing the 8-week psychotherapy course, the number accepting the second booster dose of MDMA... and adverse events'), not the drinking-behaviour data, which the Methods explicitly label a secondary outcome. Per the primary-vs-secondary boundary rule, Outcome is coded from the primary endpoint: 12/14 (85.7%) participants received both MDMA sessions (Results, 'Physiological and Tolerability Effects' section) and the Adverse Events section states no unexpected AEs occurred. No formal completion-rate statistic for the full 8-week course is given as a single number. This is a discrepancy worth flagging: the article's only SUD-related outcome (drinking units/week, TLFB) is secondary, which is why the article passes eligibility criterion (b), but Outcome itself reflects the primary safety/tolerability endpoint, not the drinking data.
article.SD: No dispersion or test statistic accompanies the primary completion/AE outcome; the study explicitly performed no hypothesis testing ('As this is a non-RTC, open label study, no hypothesis testing was performed').
article.SampleSize_NFinal: 14 is the full enrolled/dosed cohort ('14 were enrolled'; 'n=14 eligible participants who underwent the course of MDMA-assisted psychotherapy') and is the denominator for the primary completion and AE reporting.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: Design, setting (Addaction substance misuse service, Clinical Research and Imaging Centre), full inclusion/exclusion lists, intervention dosing, absence of comparator/randomization/blinding, outcomes, results, AEs, and funding/COI ('Alexander Mosely Charitable Foundation'; 'Declaration of Interests: None') are all explicitly described. Only sample_size_power fails: the article states no formal statistical/power justification for the N=14 sample beyond noting 'a relatively small sample size' as a post-hoc limitation, with no a priori or post hoc power discussion.

article.Retention (%): Study is not randomized, so the enrolled N (14) is the denominator per the non-randomized rule. Numerator is ambiguous: the clearest single completion figure reported is '12 of the fourteen participants received both sessions of MDMA-assisted psychotherapy' (85.7%). An alternative reading from the Figure 3 caption ('One participant dropped out of the study at 3-months and two patients failed to provide data at 9-month follow-up') would suggest 13/14 (92.9%) if only the formal drop-out counts as attrition. The 12/14 figure was chosen because it ties directly to completion of the core MDMA-assisted intervention, which is the study's stated primary retention-relevant outcome.
article.MediatingYN: No formal mediation analysis (indirect-effect test, causal mediation model, Baron-and-Kenny-style regression) is reported. Candidate mediators (empathy/compassion scales) were measured but the article states those results 'will be published in forthcoming papers,' so a mediator was measured but not formally tested here — this is 0 (measured, no test), not 3 (never measured). The Discussion's claims about mechanism (e.g., MDMA 'may contribute to improved self-awareness') are narrative only.
article.ModeratingYN: No formal moderation analysis (interaction term, subgroup-by-treatment interaction, stratified effect-modification test) is reported anywhere. Candidate moderators (age, sex, baseline AUD severity) were measured, so 0 (measured, no formal test) rather than 3 (never measured).
article.HypothesisTestReportedYN: Coded 0 on the explicit statement in Data Analysis: 'As this is a non-RTC, open label study, no hypothesis testing was performed.' The primary outcomes (completion counts, booster acceptance, AE occurrence) are reported purely descriptively (counts/percentages), with no p-value, CI excluding null, named test statistic, or verbal significance claim anywhere for them.
article.Power: No a priori or post hoc power calculation or discussion is present anywhere in the text. The Limitations section states only 'a relatively small sample size', which does not explicitly invoke statistical power, so this was not treated as meeting the 'bare statement of underpowered' threshold.
article.PrimaryCare: Recruitment was from a specialist community substance-misuse service (Addaction) and academic/NHS mental-health/neuropsychopharmacology centres; no interface with primary-care (GP) settings or providers is described.
article.BaseStatus: The article reports AUD severity as spanning both bands ('most eligible participants in the moderate to severe range', Figure 1/SADQ/SIP). Given the closed enum forces a single value, 'Severe' was chosen as best judgment, supported by the population's detoxification requirement and high rates of alcohol-related blackouts (64%), withdrawal seizures (14%), risky incidents (86%) and forensic history (75%). This is a genuine judgment call given the mixed 'moderate to severe' description.
article.Age_Median: Reported mean age 48 years falls in the 30-50 bracket.
article.PercentFem: 6 of 14 enrolled were female (8 males, 6 females) = 42.9%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Article states 'All were White British', so BIPOC percent = 0.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: Coded 1 based on explicit employment-status reporting (4 employed, 9 unemployed, 1 retired), i.e. 64% unemployed, describing a socioeconomically disadvantaged sample; no direct income or public-insurance figures were given.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Study conducted in the United Kingdom (Bristol/Imperial College London, North Somerset Substance Misuse Service); coded 'NonUS' per the closed-enum rule (never a literal country name in the data field).
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: 36 participants attended screening and only 14 (39%) were enrolled, reflecting extensive medical/psychiatric exclusion criteria typical of an early-phase safety trial; coded 0 as a highly screened rather than real-world representative sample.
article.Comparator/RandomizationYN/BlindingYN/Do: Open-label, single-arm, non-placebo-controlled feasibility study ('this trial... it was an open-label, non-placebo-controlled study. Therefore all patients knew they would be getting MDMA'). Per PromptVersion v1.2, these four design elements are coded 0 (absent), not 3, since the concept clearly applies to this design and was simply not implemented.
article.QualityOfLifeMeasured: Quality of life was listed as a secondary outcome and data were collected ('changes... quality of life measures... will be published in forthcoming papers'), but detailed QoL results are deferred to a future paper and not reported quantitatively here.
article.Implementation Outcome: The study's stated main outcome measures include completion of the 8-week course and acceptance of the second booster MDMA dose, which are feasibility/acceptability implementation outcomes.
article.EligibilityNote / EligibilityFailedCrite: Both coded 'NA' because EligibleYN = 'Y': the article reports a prospectively planned open-label clinical trial (criterion a) with a secondary SUD outcome (drinking units/week via TLFB, criterion b).
article.SchemaRevisionNote: 2026-09-03 schema-revision splice: ConfoundYN/PVal removed, MediatingYN/ModeratingYN/HypothesisTestReportedYN added, sourced from a separate v3 extraction run (PromptVersion v1.3) rather than this file's own v1.2 run. ae_events.Sessa 2021_AE01: Included despite being framed by the authors as an expected, benign drug effect, per the instruction not to silently absorb reported safety-monitoring findings; graded Mild because the article states values stayed within normal limits and no intervention was required for any participant except the one captured separately in AE02.
ae_events.Sessa 2021_AE02: The peak BP value (183/118) is objectively high, but the article explicitly states the participant was 'asymptomatic' and 'no medical intervention was required', and the event resolved spontaneously within two hours; graded Mild per the rubric's instruction to grade by consequence/intervention need rather than raw intensity. Withholding the scheduled booster dose was treated as a protocol/dosing decision, not a medical intervention, consistent with the authors' own framing.
ae_events.Sessa 2021_AE03: Coded as a distinct challenging_experience-type event per the instruction to flag CEQ-sense phenomenology (elevated anticipatory SUDS before dosing) rather than omit it; graded Mild as it is described as expected and self-resolving without pharmacological intervention (lorazepam was available but not stated as administered).

config_proposal.note: This is a single-arm, open-label safety/tolerability study with no comparator and no hypothesis testing performed; the primary outcome (completion/AE rates) is purely descriptive, so no standard effect-size conversion (d/g/eta_p/F/chi2/OR/RR) is defensible. The secondary drinking-behaviour data (130.6 to 18.7 units/week at 9 months) is a within-subject pre/post change with no between-groups comparator and cannot be treated as a between-groups effect size either.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Single-arm design with a favourable within-subject direction on both the primary outcome (85.7% completed both MDMA sessions, no unexpected AEs) and the secondary outcome (alcohol consumption fell from 130.6 to 18.7 units/week at 9-month follow-up; 9/14 totally abstinent).
